doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Old man Ullett, the old Creole violinist, and Manuel Perez
summary: Martin and Tom sort out Ullett versus Morett, an old Creole violinist and bandleader whose group played Franklin Street places and Bucktown. Tom played with him and recalls Cantrell with his shaky spells.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: And at that time Nam he was playing with that old man. Nam was playing with Dorsey. But later he was playing later after with Ullett. Ullett was a branch band. Ullett.
Ullett. Ullett.
Ullett. Ullett. Ullett.
Ullett. Ullett or Morett. Morett or something. Morett.
He played trumpet.
Oh yeah.
I've heard of him.
Yeah. He used to play trumpet. Well no one used to go. That was a standing man. Manuel played trumpet. Perez. Manuel Perez.
Well I don't believe Manuel was dead then. Eh? I don't believe Manuel was dead then.
Yeah, he used to play with him.
As later?
Yeah.
Maybe after Nam was dead. Who? Manuel.

No, he played with him then. I remember the old man, Ullett used to play, because he was the hardest man we had on the street. That was the hardest man. George Morett.
That's right, George Morett.
But I ain't talking about him. I'm talking about old Ullett. Ullett? Ullett. Ullett, not Morett.

That's the old Creole. Yeah, Narm used to play with him. Well? To say across the river too, Ullett, across the river. No, no, he's not. No, Ullett. Well the old man Ullett, I played with him, with, uh, in Bucktown. Yeah. With the old man Ullett. He's the old Creole man. Yeah. But he had, and this cantrip used to play, uh, uh, uh, ghetto. Cantrip. He used to have, uh, well you don't know him, then. He used to have, uh, you know he gets little spells sometimes. Oh yeah, the shaky spells. Yeah, the shaky spells. He used to play ghetto with him. Well, then, that was a good band, old man Ullett. He used to play at the Franklin Street, all them, all them little places, they had four pieces like that. He used to, mm, mm, but he was a positioner though. Well, I played with them fellas.
